deck_title: Taylor-Culick sqrt(2*sigma/(rho*h)) liquid sheet rim retraction vs naive constant-speed rupture rig

cards.subtitle: Deterministic Geoffrey Ingram Taylor (1959) & Fred E. C. Culick (1960) capillary liquid-sheet and soap-film rim retraction law (retraction velocity v_TC(h) = sqrt(2 * sigma / (rho * h)) = v_0 / sqrt(1 + u), balancing double-interface surface tension pull 2*sigma against swept rim momentum flux dm/dt * v_TC = rho * h * v_TC^2 to lock (rho*h*v^2)/(2*sigma) = 1.0000x across all 17 thickness stations h/h_0 = 1 + u in [1.000, 2.000] with 0/17 violated) versus naive constant-speed hole expansion (v = v_0, which inflates momentum flux as h/h_0 = 1 + u to 1.2500x at S4, 1.5000x at S8, and 2.0000x at S16 across 16/17 stations) and 64-step Rankine-Hugoniot rim mass-sweep quadrature.

cards.headline: Exact controls are useful; realism remains a separate job.
good_fit: Soap bubble bursting animations, crown-splash liquid sheet perforation, waterfall curtain tearing, and viscous slime rupture VFX
Scaling hole expansion velocity inversely with square root of local film thickness v_TC = sqrt(2*sigma/(rho*h)) so gravity-drained thin bubble tops zip open faster than thick bottom pools
Sizing the toroidal rim bead volume V_rim = int h(r) 2*pi*r dr from swept film mass conservation
not_for: Brittle glass shattering where crack propagation is governed by Rayleigh elastic wave speed rather than capillary tension
